patterns.name: retry
patterns.title: Retry with Backoff
patterns.intent: Re-attempt a failing asynchronous operation on a bounded, jittered schedule so a transient fault does not become a request failure.

options.name: backoff
options.description: How the delay grows between attempts. `exponential` multiplies by a factor each time, `linear` adds the base delay each time, `constant` waits the same amount every time.

options.name: jitter
options.description: How much randomness to mix into each delay, so that many clients failing together do not retry in lockstep. `full` picks anywhere from zero to the computed delay, `equal` picks from the upper half of it, `none` uses it exactly and needs no random source.

options.name: cancellation
options.description: Whether the retry loop accepts an AbortSignal, so a caller can abandon it mid-wait. `none` emits a loop with no cancellation plumbing at all.

options.name: includeTests
options.description: Emit an executable test suite alongside the implementation.

patterns.provenance: Original implementation. Exponential backoff with full and equal jitter follows the schedule described in the AWS Architecture Blog's "Exponential Backoff And Jitter" (2015), which is a published analysis rather than a codebase; the code here is written from that description.
